Margin Estimator API Client

API is the backend for the web application. REST client

  • Uniform interface: This includes commons naming protocols, consistent retrievable patterns (HTTP methods like GET, PUT, PATCH), and single-URI resource identification.

  • Client-server separation: The client applications and servers can evolve separately from each other.

  • Therefore, API clients are popular with developers because they allow them to perform API testing (as well as document, mock, etc.) that does not depend on a specific programming language.

API client tools is automation. They can automatically generate tests, requests, documentation, and libraries, bringing substantial time savings to teams working on maintaining or building APIs.

It provide full access to cpme API with already prepared functions with all data models classes prepared in python. It helpd any protorype developnemt which uses cpME for margining and it enable to generate comlex portfolios to calculate margins in form of data class models.

It is in form of simple linrary which contains adidtional tools for saving, loading and fetching snapshots from backend. Like fitelered series, loading data from json file, store messages into the json. XML, excel. (in case if indication ve margin for isntance.)

Cloud Prisma Margin Estimator (CPME) calculates margin for an uploaded portfolio according to Eurex PRISMA methodology. The application is available to both members and non-members of Eurex Clearing. It can be accessed via web user interface, see CPME GUI, or directly through API, described here. API allows to combine more input files/formats into one request, e.g.report cp005 with productive postions plus csv with additional positions.

Hint: Hint https://apispec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_core.html

github.com/marshmallow-code/apispec

Installation

Virtual environments

The main purpose of Python virtual environments is to create an isolated environment for a Python project to have its own dependencies, regardless of other projects. Read more about Python Virtual Environment Python 3 already has the venv module installed with the standard library.

Depending on your preferred Python installation. You can create virtual environment to use cpme_api client as follows:

python3 -m venv cpme-environment  # macOS/ Linux
python3 -m venv cpme-environment  # Windows

Activate this virtual environment:

source cpme-environment/bin/activate  # macOS/ Linux
cpme-environment\Scripts\activate     # Windows

To exit the environment:

deactivate

Install

clone a stable version from Github repository:

git clone https://github.deutsche-boerse.de/dev/DAVe-MarginEstimator-PythonAPIClient --depth 1 -b master

activate your virtual environment

enter to the downloaded sub folder cpme_api

cd <local_folder>/DAVe-MarginEstimator-PythonAPIClient/cpme_api

and run

pip install .

set up PYTHONPATH It must be defined anytime before you want to use the client lib!

export PYTHONPATH=<local_folder>/DAVe-MarginEstimator-PythonAPIClient

To check that api client is working just execute some example script

./example/cmpe_products_example.py

Configuration

With the instance of Configuration class in Module configuration you can set-up the api client if you do not want to use default settings.

Note

The logging to stdout is off as a default.

if you want to enable log messages into the stdout:

config = Configuration()
config.enable_logging = True

if you want to enable logging into a file just define a file name or file name with path

config.file_logger = "cpme.log"

config.file_logger = "./data/cpme.log"

Note

The set up of file_logger will enable only the file logger without stdout.

You can switch to “debug” mode which affects stdout or file logger if they are enabled.

config.debug = True

The api client returns dictionary of the JSON structure as default if there is no error. If some error on server occurs eg. error code <> 200 then an exception with error message will be triggered.

If you want to received response object of cpme_api.api.feature.rest.RESTResponse just disable the default setting:

config.enable_json = False

Important

In case of async_request=True parameter in a called function of api you will receive thread object instead. For more detailed about async request usage follows.

API Key For API access please register at Deutsche Boerse API website . There you create your project, subscribe to Prisma Margin Estimator API and get a key.

config.api_key = 'api key string'  # from DBP

Note

The api key can be explicitely defined as an optional parameter of each request function of particular api instance. The parameter api_key for instance api.securities_get(api_key=’api key string’). For more parameters see Module cpme_api.

Warning

If the API key is not valid the server send an error 401 and client raise an exception.

cpme_api.api.feature.rest.ApiException: (401) Reason: Unauthorized …

The server API url is as default static address https://risk.developer.deutsche-boerse.com/prisma-margin-estimator-2-0-0 and you do not need to define it.

config.url = 'server url'

Warning

For the proxy connection there can be some issue eg. no response and the proxy must be set up:

config.proxy = “http://my.proxy:port”

For more info about proxy connection you can follow urllib3 documentation. The client uses ProxyManager

The secure connection parameters like password, certificate you can define via properties, see Module configuration.

Sending request

The Margin Estimator API client contains functions requests defined in swagger. It’s implementations you can fine in Module cpme_api.

At first the instance of the client must be created. The connector uses ThreadPool and the connection needs to be properly finished with closed() function.

from cpme_api.api import CpmeApi

api = CpmeApi()

result = api.products_get()
...

api.close()

The parameters of proper request method are shown in doc string.

Note

There are four optional parameters which has impact only on the individual request. ‘async_req’, ‘verbose’, ‘request_timeout’, ‘api_key’

async_req=True enable asynchronous request and function returns a thread more information about async usage see ..

verbose=False Disable info messages of particular request. It is True as default.

request_timeout=5 Define timeout interval for one request.

api_key Your key, obtain it by registering at DBG Digital Business Platform (required)

All endpoints are defined in cpme_api.api.endpoints module.

GET.products                    POST.estimator
GET.series                      POST.otc_trade_details
GET.securities                  POST.otc_sensitivities
GET.clearing_currencies         POST.greeks
GET.snapshots                   POST.stressmatrix
GET.live_snapshots              POST.stress_test
GET.indicative_margin
GET.config
GET.global_scenarios

The return value is dictionary of JSON as default. The project contains example folder for the inspiration.

Get Requests

The list of supported requests with optional parameters:

clearing_currencies_get(business_date, live, live_timestamp)
indicative_margin_get(clearing_house, products, format, business_date, busness_date_from, business_date_to, live, include_components)
live_snapshots_get(business_date)
products_get(business_date, extrafields, live, live_timestamp)

All get requests function of client has _get suffix. For the first usage lets try to get products snapshot with parameter extrafields and save the message into the json file and its snaphost part into the csv file. We not use logging and pass api key via optional parameter.

from cpme_api.api import CpmeApi
from cpme_api.api.feature.utils import json_to_file, list_to_csv

api = CpmeApi()

resp =  api.products_get(extrafields=api.get_extrafields(GET.products), api_key='your api key')
json_to_file(resp, './data/products')
list_to_csv(resp['products'], './data/products')

api.close()

The files will be silently created.

Note

The function get_extrafields(endpoint: str) return all columns comma separated names. It can be used only with series_get and products_get which support optional parameter extrafields.

To enable logging use instance of Configuration class.

from cpme_api.api import CpmeApi, Configuration
from cpme_api.api.feature.utils import json_to_file

config = Configuration()
config.enable_logging = True

api = CpmeApi(configuration=config)
resp =  api.products_get(extrafields=api.get_extrafields(GET.products), api_key='your api key')
json_to_file(resp, './data/products')

api.close()

# out:

Post Requests

All post requests function of client has _post suffix and contains one mandatory parameter body which is type of dict.

Body message is complex JSON dictionary structure which can be created following ways:

  • dynamically with model data classes

  • pass simple dictionary structure to body parameter

  • load structure from json file

The first example shows part of code with simple body load to calculate margin for actual business date with estimator_post() function.

...
message = {
    "portfolio_components": [
        {
            'etd_portfolio': [
                {
                    'line_no': 1,
                    'product_id': 'FEXD',
                    'contract_date': 20301220,
                    'net_ls_balance': 1
                }
            ],
            "type": "etd_portfolio"
        }
    ]
}

result = api.estimator_post(body=message)
json_to_file(result, './data/estimator-margin')
api.close()

The example below shows body load from a json file.

from cpme_api.features import load_json_file

...
result = api.estimator_post(body=load_json_file(file_name='body_file.json'))
json_to_file(result, './data/estimator-margin')
api.close()

And last example shows dynamically created body request for estimator with etd_portfolio and otc components for some live timestamp.

"""Dynamic composition of body request of estimator with many components"""
# fetch option series 'GSK' with time to expiration <= 50
product_ids = ('GSK', 'ODAX')
series_list = get_series(prod_ids=product_ids, max_tte=50, options_only=True, api=api)

# get random timestamp for current business date
timestamp = get_live_snapshot(date=get_business_date(api=api), ts_only=True, random_flag=True, api=api)

# define estimator body
es_body = spec.BodyEstimator()
# assign Live Snapshot
es_body.snapshot = spec.Snapshot()
es_body.snapshot.live = True
es_body.snapshot.live_timestamp = timestamp
es_body.clearing_currency = 'EUR'

# Create first portfolio component for otc_csv
otc_csv_comp = spec.BodyEstimatorPortfolioComponents()

# upload data from csv file
otc_csv_comp.otc_csv = spec.OtcCsv(csv=csv_to_str('./data/requests/otc_csv.csv'))

# create second portfolio component for etd_portfolio
etd_p_comp = spec.BodyEstimatorPortfolioComponents(type='etd_portfolio')
inx = 0
for series in series_list:
    inx += 1
    # create etd_portfolio positions
    pc_etd = spec.EtdPositionsInner()
    pc_etd.line_no = inx + 1
    pc_etd.iid = series['iid']
    pc_etd.product_id = series['product_id']
    pc_etd.net_ls_balance = 20 * inx
    etd_p_comp.etd_portfolio.append(pc_etd)

# aggregate portfolio components
es_body.portfolio_components.append(otc_csv_comp)
es_body.portfolio_components.append(etd_p_comp)
es_body.fancy(line_text='BODY:')

# send request
response = api.estimator_post(body=es_body.to_dict())

# show and save result message
fancy(response, 'RESP:')
json_to_file(response, './data/estimator_etd_otc')

For more information about manipulation with models/data classes see section How to use model library

Tools and useful functions

The client library contains two moduls with useful function which speed up writing request scripts.

cpme_api.api.utils module

fancy(json_dict: dict, line_text: str = ‘’)

  • Pretty print of dict or list structure as a JSON format into stdout only!

json_to_file(data_dict: Union[dict, list], file_name: str, verbose=True, update=True) -> str

  • Save dictionary structure into the JSON file.

    • data_dict: dictionary object of json response

    • file_name: The file_name can be string with absolute (‘/.’) or relative (‘./’) path or just a file name.

    • verbose: if False disable information messages

    • update: if True it overwrites already existing file

    • return: absolute path of file_name

csv_to_str(path: str) -> str

  • Returns content of csv file as a string.

list_to_csv(rows: list, file_name: str)

  • Save list of dict into the file_name.

load_json_file(file_dir: str = ‘’, file_name: str = ‘’, path: str = None, verbose: bool = False) -> dict

  • Load JSON data into dict.

cpme_api.api.tools modules

get_business_date(prev=False, all_dates=False, api: CpmeApi = None) -> Union[int, List[int]]:

  • returns current business date as default if no optional parameters

  • all_dates = True returns list of all business dates

  • prev = True returns previous business date

  • api is user instance of CpmeApi with proper configuration

get_live_snapshot(date: int, ts_only=False, random_flag=False, api: CpmeApi = None) -> Union[dict, int]:

  • api is user instance of CpmeApi with proper configuration

  • date YYYYMMDD

  • When ts_only=True and random_flag=True = return only one timestamp

  • When ts_only=False and random_flag=True = return list of timestamps

  • otherwise it returns live_snapshot records, eg:

business_date,cash_available,live,live_timestamp,otc_available
20220906,True,True,0,True
20220906,True,True,1662423998525,True

get_series(prod_ids, date, max_len, max_tte, futures_only, options_only, flex, api, verbose)

  • Returns filtered series of the market with conditions.

    • prod_ids: list of product eg. (‘ODAX’, ‘FDAX’)

    • date: business date as int YYYYMMDD

    • max_len: Then number of returned series

    • max_tte: Filter series with time_to_expiration <= max_tte

    • futures_only: bool Returns only futures instruments.

    • options_only: bool Returns only options instruments.

    • flex: bool assume flex instruments

    • api is user instance of CpmeApi with proper configuration

    • verbose: bool disable notification of progress to stdout

Parallel requests

The client support asynchronous request with optional parameter async_req. The called function returns thread with auto assign id. There is thread attribute ready() which is True if the response is fetched.

You can follow example script for more information script

How to use model library

The library contains classes with properties and auto initialization of nested structures called models. The models are split into main three namespaces

  • primitive: data models of string, integers

  • request_body: data models of body messages

  • responses:

The data models is located in .cpme_api/models and they can be acces with simple import cpme_api.models as spec There is access to request_body and responses namespace.

If we want to see reponse structure of series

Every class contains theses functions:
